“Neumorphism and CSS”

A March 2020 CSS-Tricks article that turned the style into CSS and set it against Material Design.

Source
CSS-Tricks
Creator
Adrian Bece
Made
2020 (published 20 March 2020)
Style
Neumorphism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Soft
Evidence
Text read from the live page on 2026-09-28; the date is from its article:published_time metadata. Figures and demos were not inspected.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The article says the style “got its name in a UX Collective post from December 2019” (Malewicz) and that “Adam Giebl created an online generator for it” (neumorphism.io).

Its comparison table: in Material Design “elements have a single or multiple dark shadows around them”; in neumorphism “elements have two shadows: one light and one dark”. Background colors “must be the same (or very similar) as the background color of the parent element”, and “rounded edges are a defining quality”.

It allows an “optional subtle border to improve contrast”, and credits Alexander Plyuto with having “championed and evolved neomorphic designs on his Dribbble account”.

Why it belongs

Evidence that by March 2020 the style had moved from Dribbble concepts into web practice, with CSS box-shadow pairs as its standard implementation.
